chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ali b. al-Salt narrated to us from his uncle Abdullah b. al-Salt from Yunus b. Abd al-Rahman from Amr b. Shimr from Jabir b. Yazid al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him).

He said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Messenger (may God's blessings be upon him and his family): I have thanked Ja'far b. Abi Talib for four characteristics. So the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) called for him and informed him.

He said: Had Allah not informed you, I would not have informed you. I have never drunk wine, because I knew that if I were to drink it, my intellect would depart. And I have never lied, because lying diminishes chivalry. And I have never committed adultery, because I feared that if I did it, it would be done to me. And I have never worshipped an idol, because I knew that it neither harms nor benefits.

He said: Then the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) placed his hand on his shoulder and said: It is Allah's right, the Mighty and Majestic, to give you two wings with which you may fly with the angels in Paradise.

key_terms.المروءة: chivalry — manly virtue, honor, and noble character
key_terms.جناحين: two wings — the wings God granted Ja'far in Paradise
key_terms.صنم: idol — a false deity worshipped besides God

ai.seo_question: What are the four characteristics for which God thanked Ja'far ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (as) recounts that God revealed to the Prophet (s) that He thanked Ja'far b. Abi Talib for four noble qualities he possessed even before Islam: abstaining from wine to preserve intellect, avoiding lying to maintain honor, refusing adultery out of moral reciprocity, and rejecting idol worship due to its futility. This teaching was given in the context of pre-Islamic Arabia, where Ja'far's self-discipline was extraordinary. The Prophet rewarded him with the glad tidings that God would grant him two wings to fly with the angels in Paradise — earning him the epithet Ja'far al-Tayyar (the Flyer).
